paper.title: WebRL: Training LLM Web Agents via Self-Evolving Online Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: WebRL trains open LLM web-agent policies through failure-seeded self-evolving curricula, an outcome reward model, KL-constrained reinforcement learning and confidence-filtered replay, achieving continuing gains and superior WebArena-Lite success.
paper.scope_class: out_of_scope: evaluated improvement resides in trained policy weights; generated training tasks and replay are training intermediates, not a retained deployment harness modification

provenance.notes: Assigned model type sonnet maps to gpt-6.1-sol; environment identifies gpt-6.1-sol. No independent runtime receipt or session identifier exposed; actual_model left null per worker template. No model probing.

sections_read: Complete fixed HTML text lines 1–5187: abstract, §§1–5, all Tables 1–7, Appendix A derivation/proof/comparison, B training details and complete Algorithm 1, C additional experiments, D prompt descriptions, E qualitative-example captions. Several figures/prompts are image-only in HTML; no page_images supplied. No unrendered figure numbers/contents invented; central update-object determination is explicit in text and Algorithm 1.

evidence.quote: In each training phase, novel tasks are autonomously generated from unsuccessful attempts in the preceding phase, facilitating a progressive learning trajectory.
evidence.support_explanation: Failure feedback changes training-task distribution; does not by itself establish persistent harness improvement.

evidence.quote: is utilized to assess whether the agent’s rollout trajectory accomplishes a given task, providing a binary reward signal (0 for failure and 1 for success).
evidence.support_explanation: Learned ORM supplies training feedback, not a self-revised non-weight evaluator.

evidence.quote: We select instructions the model failed to complete in previous interaction phases as seeds for generating new instructions.
evidence.support_explanation: Real measured failures steer GPT-4o task generation.

evidence.quote: We select instructions with critic scores between 0.05 and 0.75, ensuring that only tasks meeting our difficulty criteria are retained.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention is of training instructions selected by critic difficulty, not admission of a harness component for future task execution.

evidence.quote: Specifically, we only store those successful trajectories (which can be sparse) from each phase in the replay buffer.
evidence.support_explanation: Non-weight persistent buffer exists, but its consumer is actor/critic parameter training rather than inference retrieval.

evidence.quote: Actions with a perplexity within the range of 1/0.95 to 1/0.5, along with their corresponding states, are added to the training data for the current phase.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicitly identifies historical experience as training data; prevents conflating replay with deployed agent memory.

evidence.quote: achieves an average accuracy of 42.4%, surpassing all baselines, including prompting and training alternatives.
evidence.support_explanation: Author reports trained-policy result, not retained tool/prompt/workflow effect.

evidence.quote: Both newly generated interaction data on these instructions and historical data with perplexity between 1/0.95 and 1/0.5 from the replay buffer are used to train the actor and critic.
evidence.support_explanation: Decisive evaluated-update-object evidence: actor and critic trained from generated and replayed data.

evidence.quote: utilizing only the instructions generated in the first phase.
evidence.support_explanation: Curriculum ablation still measures weight-training outcomes, not utility of a modified deployed harness.

evidence.quote: We conduct four sets of experiments, each utilizing a distinct random seed.
evidence.support_explanation: Paper does report multi-seed evidence; scope exclusion must not be mistaken for a criticism that experiments are wholly absent.

evidence.quote: However, in the case of Map, there is an initial upward trend followed by a decline.
evidence.support_explanation: Continual improvement is not monotonic on each website; outside-scope disposition does not erase author negative outcomes.
ORM is trained on labeled trajectories with reward-function anchors; this is trained reward modeling, not a retained textual evaluator revision.

signatures.object: Generated curriculum instruction sets I_n, failed-task set F, actor/critic weights
signatures.information: Previous failed rollouts as judged by ORM; critic initial-state scores; GPT-4o feasibility filtering
signatures.operation: Generate new instructions from failures; filter difficulty 0.05–0.75 and feasibility; rollout current policy; train actor and critic; repeat eight phases.
signatures.output: New training tasks and improved web-policy model checkpoints
signatures.conditions: Valid generated tasks, calibrated critic/reward, controlled policy drift
signatures.feedback: Trained binary ORM, initially anchored with WebArena-Lite reward functions
signatures.selection_rule: Critic difficulty band and GPT-4o feasibility screen, 500 instructions per phase
signatures.selection_data: Training-set failures and generated-task rollouts; test is 165 WebArena-Lite cases
signatures.persistence: Failure archive and training curricula across phases; actor/critic parameter updates
signatures.later_use: Updated policy executes later web tasks; tasks supply training, not inference-time conditioning/reusable harness routines
signatures.claimed_effect: Llama3.1-8B success 4.8→42.4%; SFT 20.6→WebRL 42.4 on Lite; GLM9B 43.0, Llama70B49.1
signatures.failure_boundary: Proxy reward errors, generated-task feasibility, site-level forgetting; importantly improved retained evaluated agent is weight-trained

signatures.information: ORM success and last actor action perplexity
signatures.operation: Store successes; choose moderate-perplexity actions; mix with current rollouts at historical-data cap twice interaction size; train actor/critic with KL-constrained policy loss
signatures.output: Replay-derived training batches and new weights
signatures.conditions: Reward label reliability and value estimation; neither trivial nor excessively hard past samples
signatures.feedback: Binary task outcomes and policy likelihood
signatures.later_use: Gradient training, not deployment memory retrieval
signatures.claimed_effect: Avoid catastrophic forgetting and improve multi-phase weight learning
signatures.failure_boundary: Performance drops on Map; failed replay can hurt intermediate-action estimates

gap.author_gap: Open web agents lack tasks and decision capability; sparse long-horizon reward and policy distribution drift limit online RL.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete training limitations and a failure-steered curriculum are specified, with SFT, Filtered BC, AWR and DigiRL comparisons; these concern weight-level agent training, not the current collection’s non-weight harness object.

claims.text: Self-evolving curriculum RL improves trained open web agents.
claims.setting: 165-case WebArena-Lite, five websites, Llama3.1 8B/70B and GLM4 9B.
claims.baseline/control: SFT, Filtered BC, AWR, DigiRL; curriculum/replay/KL ablations; prompt-only proprietary baselines and some full-WebArena literature numbers.
claims.selection_vs_test: Training tasks are seed-derived/generated; success measured on Lite test. Independent detailed overlap not audited here; some figure-only prompts unavailable.
claims.result/denominator: Llama8B WebRL42.4 vs SFT20.6/DigiRL30.3; GLM9B43.0 vs SFT22.4/DigiRL31.5; Llama70B49.1 vs SFT23.0. Paper reports four seeds and some site-level regression.
counterevidence: Cross-benchmark full versus Lite literature comparisons are not strictly matched
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported improvement of trained web-policy weights with adaptive curriculum; not evidence of retained non-weight harness self-improvement.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Weight-trained policies achieve higher reported WebArena-Lite task success. Retained replay/curriculum serve parameter learning; no retained non-weight deployment artifact or improver-level harness improvement demonstrated. Scope exclusion is not a quality verdict on RL science.
